transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start time: 12:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Emma Rodriguez, Kai Nguyen, Jordan Lee, Maya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Zara Patel, plus ~140 others on the call.

Summary (auto): weekly brown-bag — strategy and risk. Quick demo of cost dashboard v1, then SLA spotlight for Dedicated product, then live Q&A.

[00:00] Emma R: All right everyone, welcome to the Strategy Sherpa brown-bag, nice to see so many faces. I know it's lunchtime—thanks for joining. We have a compact agenda, three big things: Q2 bets, a short product demo, and a risk spotlight about Dedicated SLAs. We'll leave 15ish for Q&A.

[00:18] Kai N: Quick note, audio is a bit laggy for me, somebody said they're seeing some--

[00:22] Unknown: (inaudible)

[00:30] Emma R: Cool, Kai, you can jump in on the demo. Jordan's btw gonna talk priorities. Jordan, take it away on the bets.

[00:36] Jordan L: Thanks. So we're proposing we focus Q2 on three shipping bets: 1) Cost & observability kit — improved cost per-token visibility and actionable rules; 2) Private deployment hardening — VPC/on-prem security work + audit trails; 3) Runtime efficiency — targeted kernel optimizations for medium-length chat workloads. We looked at a bunch of inputs—benchmarks, customer asks, churn signals. The idea is pick the smallest set that move revenue and reliability.

[01:05] Maya S: Quick clarification—by runtime efficiency, do you mean we re-prioritize the kernel backlog or launch an infra-level experiment? Because that affects headcount and ops hours.

[01:14] Jordan L: Good point. We mean a two-sprint experiment to validate 2x-ish latency improvements for 95th perc on chat tails. If it looks promising we scale.

[01:23] Kai N: And to be explicit, this aligns with the work we've been doing on compilation/kernel selection. If we can show sample tokens cost reductions we can feed it into Redwood Optimize recommendations.

[01:35] Emma R: I want to underscore — this is a prioritization conversation, not final sign-off. We need leadership to agree to the set so Eng can plan.

[01:43] Liam O: From ops POV, the Dedicated SLA risks around resource preemption came up in the last support rotation. We should discuss that in the risk spotlight.

[01:52] Emma R: Ok let's pivot to the demo — Kai, you have the cost dashboard prototype?

[02:00] Kai N: Yep. Sharing screen. Uh, can people see the prototype? Maybe give a thumbs up in chat.

[02:06] Speaker 12: yes

[02:09] Kai N: Great. This is v1 of the cost/latency dashboard we've been iterating on. Top left is per-route token spend, top right is model variant cost difference, middle shows an anomalies pane where we surface spike reasons (e.g., long sequences, bad batching). At the bottom is a rule-builder for recommendations — say, suggest 8-bit quantized variant for batchable workloads or enable prefix caching for high-repeat sessions.

[02:37] (15s gap in transcript; audio drop)

[02:52] Kai N: Sorry, dropped for a sec. Continuing — the idea is to tie this to per-customer billing rows and to surface a conservative estimate of potential monthly savings if a recommended action is applied. It's intentionally prescriptive.

[03:07] Jordan L: Love the 'savings per action' view. We should be careful with phrasing: "potential savings" vs guaranteed. Legal got nervous last time we displayed projected billing numbers without guardrails.

[03:20] Kai N: Agreed, we'll show ranges and a confidence score.

[03:24] Emma R: Good. That prototype also helps sales — they can show customers grounded recommendations during an adoption POC.

[03:32] Maya S: On the infra side, I want to know how much of the data powering these views is sampled. If we use heavy sampling we'll miss tail cases and the recommendations could be noisy.

[03:45] Kai N: Currently it's a mix — full telemetry for hosted API, sampling for Dedicated. Roadmap item to extend sampling fidelity for Dedicated in Q2 if we commit.

[03:55] Emma R: Ok, thanks. Now the risk spotlight — Liam?

[04:00] Liam O: Thanks. So recent Dedicated customer runs have exposed two risk threads: 1) SLA ambiguity around preemption and cold-starts when we autoscale pools; 2) Contract terms that reference latency SLOs without explicit mitigation steps. A quick example: a customer experienced a 15% throughput drop during a maintenance window and their contract wording didn't map to our fallback policy. That opens us to credit exposure.

[04:35] Zara P: Are we seeing any churn signals tied to this?

[04:38] Liam O: Not yet major churn; mostly escalations and a couple of support credits. But if top 5 customers push for clearer SLOs, legal will want standardized mitigation playbooks.

[04:47] Emma R: So practically: we need an SLA playbook: clear definitions (what's a breach), tiers of mitigation, and automated detection + rollback/fallback mechanisms. Maya and Liam to lead with Legal on the wording.

[05:00] Maya S: On detection, Eng can emit a "pool degradation" signal in telemetry. It won't be perfect day one but it helps automate remediation.

[05:07] Liam O: Exactly. Also recommend adding a clause about "operationally reasonable efforts to mitigate" and allow scheduled maintenance windows. Legal to validate wording.

[05:18] Emma R: Jordan, will this change any roadmap commitments?

[05:22] Jordan L: Potentially. If we need to add telemetry and remediation work to Dedicated, that competes with runtime efficiency experiment. I propose we treatmentize (sic) these as overlapping: invest a small fraction of kernel time to support better failover. I will reprioritize and surface tradeoffs.

[05:40] Emma R: Cool. Ok quick pulse on hiring — Zara?

[05:44] Zara P: We're recommending a temporary freeze on non-essential hiring for two weeks to give us runway to fund SLA and cost work. Exceptions: revenue-critical SDRs and hard-skill infra hires approved by me. I'll post a doc with the list.

[05:58] Emma R: Thanks. Any immediate questions before Q&A?

[06:03] (silence)

[06:08] Emma R: All right let's move to Q&A — type questions in chat or raise hand. I'll moderate.

[06:15] Speaker 18: Quick question — will the cost dashboard be exposed to customers or internal only?

[06:21] Kai N: Internally first. We'll expose a curated subset to customers via the Console; full raw view will remain internal.

[06:27] Speaker 23: Can we get more detail on the kernel experiment — is that disruptive to current infra?

[06:33] Maya S: The early experiment is non-invasive — feature flags and A/B routing to a canary runtime. If we see regressions we rollback. There is some risk for tail latency but we'll run it on synthetic workloads first.

[06:46] Speaker 27: SLA question — does this imply changes to our Dedicated pricing?

[06:50] Liam O: Not necessarily. Any big pricing change would be a commercial discussion. For now, we're tightening definitions and building automation to avoid credits. If that reduces our operational burden we can revisit pricing alignment later.

[07:06] Emma R: Ok. Two audience questions that seem similar: how do we communicate Q2 bets to customers? Jordan?

[07:13] Jordan L: We'll craft a short external narrative focused on reliability and cost predictability. Not a product roadmap leak—more like themes. Marketing and Growth to approve copy.

[07:25] Speaker 31: Are we still investing in benchmarks vs AtlasAI? Heard some sales folks using their low-latency numbers...

[07:31] Kai N: We are. We have an internal benchmarking project and a public benchmark plan for the end of Q2. We'll call out apples-to-apples configs; we don't want to get drawn into noisy comparisons but we should show repeatable workloads.

[07:48] Emma R: Great. Time check — ~20 minutes left. Last chunk of questions then we wrap.

[07:54] Speaker 36: Curious about the hiring pause—would that impact our ability to deliver the kernel work?

[07:59] Zara P: The pause is narrow; infra-critical hires are exceptions. If Eng has immediate needs, raise a request in #hiring-requests and I'll triage.

[08:10] Speaker 40: Request for more detailed cost drilldowns per model variant — sales needs that for customer renewal conversations. Is that doable?

[08:16] Kai N: Yes, it's on the roadmap for the dashboard. We'll surface a per-model variant table with token cost delta and example transcripts that drove the delta. Privacy filtered, of course.

[08:28] (small crosstalk / someone laughs)

[08:32] Emma R: Ok I'm seeing a handful of long-form questions — we'll follow up in the thread and record answers. Before closing: decisions and owners recap.

[08:40] Emma R: Decision 1: Q2 three bets (cost kit, private hardening, runtime experiment) to be provisionally prioritized. Decision 2: Initiate SLA playbook and telemetry work. Decision 3: Temporary narrow hiring pause.

[08:59] Emma R: Owners recap: Jordan to publish reprioritized roadmap, Maya & Liam & Legal to own SLA playbook and detection signals, Kai to share the dashboard recording and prototype link, Zara to publish hiring pause exceptions, Emma will convene a follow-up on Friday to confirm resource reallocation.

[09:20] Emma R: Any objections? (pause) Hearing none. Thank you all. We'll post notes and action items in the leadership channel and the #all-hands recaps.

[09:30] Speaker 52: Thanks Emma, good session.

[09:33] (meeting winds down, people drop)

[09:40] End of recording.
